current_hypothesis: A genuinely different way to get an explicit smooth Hamiltonian is to use compactly supported local affine symplectic pieces: if affine scalings and translations can already pack well, they would give a direct Hamiltonian-piece route without the toric singularity issue.
stop_reason: Attempt 004 ruled out the affine local-piece route as a serious candidate: exact k=10 ratio only about 0.0364 and square-case k=16 ratio only about 0.0232, so the next work should return to genuinely nonlinear smooth constructions.

last_summary.worked: Implemented src/affine_rectangular_packing.py, a new constructive family based on affine symplectic block maps and q-plane rectangle packing. Added an exact trust-region radius computation for each affine-image ball, so the family can be evaluated without relying only on boundary samples. For k=10, the best searched affine layout used the partition 1+1+1+3+4 and achieved exact radius 4.06997615255347 with exact ratio 0.03644454577737161; the sampled ratio 0.036590628028580714 matched closely. For k=16, the best searched affine layout achieved exact ratio 0.023226658924689562 with sampled ratio 0.02338864772419216. These results are reproducible in results/research_loop/affine_rectangular_packing_k10.json and results/research_loop/affine_rectangular_packing_k16.json.
last_summary.did_not_work: The affine local-piece family failed decisively as a serious solution path. Even in the square case k=16, where the toric family packs exactly, the affine family only reached ratio about 0.0232. For k=10 its exact ratio 0.03644 is only about 5.26% of the toric attempt_003 ratio 0.69252, although it is about 2.94x better than the repository's failed polynomial Hamiltonian audit ratio 0.012385. So the main obstruction is structural: affine scalings enlarge the long axes linearly and do not reproduce the square-root compression mechanism that made the toric family competitive.
last_summary.next_step: Drop purely affine local Hamiltonian pieces and return to genuinely nonlinear smooth constructions, especially regularized action-angle or slit-disk charts, or non-affine folding constructions that can preserve the square-root radius scaling.
